title: Raspberry Pi SD Card Wear Warning
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`), uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=rpi:metric
| stats latest(sd_card_wear_pct) as wear_pct, latest(io_error_count) as io_errors by host
| where wear_pct>80 OR io_errors>0
| sort - wear_pct
description: Uses SD-card wear and I/O errors as an early-warning signal for the most common Raspberry Pi failure mode in long-lived homelab setups.
value: Single-board computers are charming right up until their boot media dies; this turns that risk into something you can replace proactively.
implementation: Forward storage wear counters or smart export equivalents from each Pi; review weekly and reimage aging cards before they fail.
visualization: Table of Pi hosts by SD-card wear and I/O error count.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces which Raspberry Pi memory cards are getting worn out before they die and take a service with them.
